title: Unresolved merge anchor
description: Layout-quality rule — a text object carries a merge-field anchor (<<Field>>) that FileMaker cannot resolve. Such an anchor is not dropped: it renders LITERALLY in browse and preview mode, so the user sees the raw <<Field>> where a value belongs. It also leaves no trace in the catalog — no displays_field edge, no object of its own — which makes this rule the only place it becomes visible. Detection compares the anchors in the text (merge variables <<$…>> and layout calculations <<ƒ:…>> excluded, a repetition or a TO qualification counting as one anchor) against the FieldReference entries of the object's structural FieldList, which holds exactly one entry per resolved anchor. Counting decides the finding; the named suspects are a best effort and stay empty when the names cannot be matched safely.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: The anchor shows its own source text to the user instead of data. Nothing errors and nothing logs — a renamed or deleted field leaves the layout looking broken in a way only a reader notices. Text deliberately written in angle brackets (<<see note>>) lands here too: FileMaker renders it literally for the same reason.
rule.remediation: Point the anchor at an existing field (watch the table occurrence: <<TO::Field>> needs a TO of this layout's graph), or remove it. If the angle brackets were meant as prose, reword them.
